questions.q: What is the default interaction behavior between visuals on a Power BI report page?
options: Visuals have no effect on each other unless explicitly configured
Only visuals on the same table interact
Every visual cross-filters and cross-highlights every other visual automatically
Interactions must be manually enabled for every pair of visuals before any interaction works
questions.explain: Out of the box, selecting a data point in one visual cross-filters and cross-highlights the others — no setup required.

questions.q: How do you see and change how a specific visual affects the others on the page?
options: Select the visual, then Format > Edit interactions
Right-click the report background and select Interactions
This can only be configured in the Power BI service, never in Desktop
Open the Filters pane
questions.explain: Edit interactions, found on the Format ribbon, reveals per-visual Filter/Highlight/None icons for controlling exactly how the selected visual affects each other one.

questions.q: What's the difference between the Filter and Highlight interaction options?
options: Filter only works on charts; Highlight only works on tables
Highlight permanently changes the data; Filter is temporary
They are identical — just two names for the same behavior
Filter hides non-matching data in the other visual; Highlight emphasizes matching data while dimming the rest, without hiding anything
questions.explain: Filter narrows what's shown; Highlight keeps everything visible but emphasizes the selection — the same distinction as cross-filter vs. cross-highlight from Lesson 54.

questions.q: Which visual types can only be cross-filtered, never cross-highlighted?
options: Line charts, scatter charts, and maps
Tables and matrices
Cards and KPIs
Slicers and buttons
questions.explain: This is a limitation specific to those visual types — not a toggle you can change, unlike the Filter/Highlight/None choice available for most other visuals.

questions.q: By default, does drilling into a visual affect other visuals on the same page?
options: Only if the visual is a table
Drilling is disabled by default across the entire report
No — drilling has no effect on other visuals by default, though this can be changed
Yes, always, with no way to turn it off
questions.explain: Drilling stays contained to its own visual by default. Setting 'Apply drill down filters to' > Entire page changes that, making drill actions update the whole page.
